hellberg.tagline: Makes hearing and face protection as a brand within Hultafors Group.

industry.text: Personal protective equipment (hearing and head protection)

parent.text: Hultafors Group, owned by Investment AB Latour

about.text: Hellberg Safety was founded in Sweden in 1962. At its acquisition by Latour in 2018, the acquirer described its own R&D, production, assembly and warehouse operations at the Stenkullen headquarters, presence in 50 markets, net sales of SEK 66 m in 2017 and around 20 employees.

The range includes passive hearing protectors and, since the early 2010s, electronic models in the Secure range with FM radio and active listening; the first Hellberg Bluetooth hearing protectors were introduced by 2014.
Hellberg Junior is a hearing protector designed for children, which the company positions for school and hobby activities, concerts, lawn mowing and sporting events.
Product listings show the Junior children's hearing protector on sale at Swedish retailers Bauhaus and Kjell & Company.

Hultafors Group describes Hellberg as aiming to provide users with "Peace of Mind" and as positioning itself to become one of the top three head protection brands in Europe; the group states a focus on professionals.

products.description: Passive hearing protectors, including the Junior headband model designed for children.
products.customers: Children, for school and hobby activities, concerts, lawn mowing and sporting events

First Hellberg Bluetooth hearing protectors introduced.

positioning.text: Hultafors Group states that Hellberg is positioning itself to become one of the top three head protection brands in Europe.
A 2021 qualitative study identified a lack of prompts to use earplugs and poor availability of earplugs as intervention targets in noisy recreational settings.
A 2015 study of musician earplugs found that users' appreciation depended mainly on comfort and looks, while differences in sound quality were less noticeable.
The American Academy of Pediatrics notes that infants and young children cannot remove themselves from noisy situations and must rely on adults to do so.
A 2026 sleep study found that earplugs mitigated nearly all effects of intermittent environmental noise on sleep, but started failing at the highest level tested (65 dBA).

neumann.tagline: Makes studio microphones, studio monitors, headphones and audio interfaces as part of the Sennheiser group.

about.text: Neumann states that few recordings, whether classical, rock or pop, television or radio, do not feature at least one Neumann microphone.
With its first audio interface, the MT 48, the company states it now offers the technologies to capture audio from sound recording to sound reproduction.

Sound On Sound (2010) reported that Neumann had not built cheaper models in the Far East, and that its TLM range includes affordable microphones aimed at the project-studio market as well as professional studio and broadcast use.

Neumann sells microphones, headphones, the MA 1 Multichannel Extension and accessories directly on its website, and runs the Neumann Home Studio Academy, a tutorial site with an associated YouTube channel.
After Sennheiser sold its consumer electronics business to Sonova in 2021, Sennheiser said it would focus entirely on pro audio, business communications and the Neumann brand.

positioning.text: Futuresource data reported in 2019 that the home studio segment was responsible for more than half of total studio vertical revenue.

A 2024 Futuresource survey reported that the home-studio content-creation equipment market had to re-stabilise from pandemic levels, with reduced consumer spending pressuring revenues in 2022 and 2023.

The same survey saw opportunities for higher-end purchases by established music and video creators, and at the lower end among less experienced users, particularly in ease of use, despite pressure from consumer and e-commerce brands.
Sound On Sound (2010) noted that the TLM 102 does not compete with the budget microphones that had flooded the market, while not being unduly expensive for a Neumann.
MusicRadar (2021) described the TLM 102 as suited to the committed home studio owner upgrading from starter gear to pro-level equipment.

jotun.tagline: Makes decorative paints and marine, protective and powder coatings.

case_context.note: Sources dated after mid-2024 describe later events and were not available at the case date.

about.text: Jotun is a Norwegian multinational paint and coatings company dealing mainly in decorative paints and performance coatings (marine, protective and powder coatings).
Its Marine Coatings business serves the new-build, dry-dock, tank and cargo holds, and sea-stock markets, and also provides coatings for mega-yachts and leisure yachts.

Jotun Decorative supplies coatings for commercial buildings, public buildings and homes, serving professional and DIY customers directly and through a network of Jotun Multicolor Centers. In 2023 Decorative Paints accounted for 37% of sales and Powder Coatings for 7%.
The company reports more than 10 000 Multicolor machines worldwide, and attributes the seasonality of its cash flow especially to sales of exterior decorative paints in Scandinavia.
In its Q2 2024 update, Jotun reported double-digit underlying sales growth year to date in Marine, Protective and Powder, with Decorative sales growing at a more modest pace.

positioning.text: Jotun reported that demand for decorative paints in Scandinavia continued to be soft due to higher interest rates affecting real estate and consumer demand, and strong sales during the pandemic years.
A 2016 study of leisure boats found that 21% of boat owners did not know what type of paint their boats were coated with.
The same study found that 14% of boat owners admitted using paints not allowed in the area studied.
Folksam's 2018 exterior paint test concluded that good paint products can be produced at a reasonable price.
On a Norwegian homeowners' forum (2012), one user said they would not risk an unfamiliar exterior paint without good independent tests, while another said they had used Jotun products for years.

tanita.tagline: Tokyo maker of weighing instruments, including bathroom and commercial scales, and of body-fat analysers using bioelectrical impedance.

industry.text: Weighing instruments and body composition analysers

case_context.note: Sources dated after 1993 describe later events and were not available at the case date.

about.text: According to its company history, Tanita obtained a scale manufacturing licence and began producing health meters (bathroom scales) in 1959, and reached 10 million health meters in 1979.

Japanese Wikipedia states that Tanita was the first company in Japan to make and sell household scales, which it named "health meters", and that it formerly worked mainly as an OEM contract manufacturer with few own-brand products.

Tanita states that, based on medical evidence linking excess body fat to heart disease, diabetes and certain cancers, it introduced the world's first integrated body composition analyzer/scale to professional markets in 1992.
US patent US5415176A (priority 1991-11-29, granted 1995-05-16) describes a body-fat apparatus that measures the impedance between a patient's feet together with height and weight.

products.description: Integrated body composition analyzer and scale, introduced to professional markets in 1992.

products.name: Precision electronic scales
products.description: Electronic scales, the category in which the company claims almost half of its domestic market.

markets.text: United States, through Tanita Corp. of America

timeline.event: Obtains a scale manufacturing licence and begins producing health meters.
Reaches 10 million health meters.
Priority date of US patent US5415176A for a foot-to-foot body-fat measuring apparatus.
Introduces an integrated body composition analyzer/scale to professional markets.
US patent US5415176A granted.
British Journal of Nutrition publishes an evaluation of the Tanita body-fat analyser against a four-compartment model.
A study advises against using the Tanita TBF-310 with the manufacturer's equations for individual overweight and obese children.

positioning.text: A 1985 study described bioelectrical impedance as safe, noninvasive and rapid, requiring little operator skill, while recommending further validation in subjects with abnormal body composition.
A 1990 study of athletes indicated the need for controlled measurement conditions to obtain valid body composition estimates by bioelectrical impedance.
The body-fat patent notes that a body's impedance varies with date, time and body condition before measurement, which can make inferred body fat inaccurate.
Japan's National Nutrition Survey showed the prevalence of preobese men rising from 14.5% in 1976-80 to 20.5% in 1991-95 (published 2002).
Current US rules exempt body composition analyzers not intended to diagnose or treat a medical condition from premarket notification (text amended 2019).

deere.tagline: Illinois maker of farm tractors, combines and industrial equipment sold through a network of independent dealers.

case_context.note: Sources dated after 1962 describe later events and were not available at the case date.

about.text: Deere sells through independent retail dealers; according to Wikipedia, Charles Deere began introducing marketing centers and independent dealers in 1869 to extend sales nationwide.
Of the "10" series tractors introduced in 1960, the 4010 was the most popular, with more than 58,000 units sold from 1960 to 1963.
Deere entered outdoor power equipment late; before it offered lawn and garden tractors, many John Deere dealers sold other brands of them.

Recollections of Deere staff describe a prototype lawn and garden tractor built at the Horicon plant in 1959, a feasibility study for an 'estate tractor' at the Industrial Equipment Works, and purchases of competing lawn and garden tractors for evaluation.
Production of the company's first lawn and garden tractor, the 110, began at Horicon in 1963 with 1000 units (after the case date).

timeline.event: Charles Deere begins introducing marketing centers and independent retail dealers.

positioning.text: A lawn and garden tractor history notes that John Deere entered the outdoor power arena late in the game.
International Harvester introduced the Cub Cadet in 1961, and Wheel Horse, Bolens and Simplicity were described as dominant players before John Deere entered.
Demand for garden tractors was rapidly increasing as households with small gardens found them inexpensive, practical for a variety of chores and economical to maintain.
By 1960, US homeownership topped 60 percent, driven by the post-war economic boom, favourable tax laws and easier mortgage financing.
Deere's development work found that a hydrostatic drive for variable ground speed had advantages but was cost prohibitive to be competitive in the marketplace.
